title: Architecture is a tested deliverable before feature volume

nodes.summary: Clean rebuild; review each boundary's types and effects before implementing
nodes.detail: Start a clean implementation porting ideas and tests, not prototype package structure. Before implementing a boundary review its public types, effect dependencies, handler composition, failure semantics and one authored example, and remove speculative fast paths, alternate implementations and unused interfaces.

realised.evidence: Implementation PRs from #6 onward are reviewed per boundary and repeatedly drop placeholders (no placeholder failure variants in #7, BuildOptions removed in #8)

nodes.summary: Layered tests with real process/Git faults; failure paths per slice
nodes.detail: Checks span pure properties, contract round trips, compile-fail boundary examples, deterministic interpreters, real process/Git fault tests and clean installs; simulation never substitutes for native integration and routine tests never hit providers. Every slice proves its failure behaviour (failed examples, guest crash, cancellation, non-compiling proposed code as pre-candidate rejection, no acquisition rerun on check/accept).

realised.evidence: Real Git/process tests from seq 7 and 22; PR #44 adds the installed CLI journey with compiler-rejection and repair cases

nodes.summary: Slice 1: package DAG and signatures with forbidden imports checked
nodes.detail: First accept boundary decisions and compile a tiny package DAG and operation signatures with forbidden imports checked, without empty capability implementations pretending the product exists.

realised.evidence: tools/checks/check-imports.mjs first appears with the first implementation PR at seq 6

nodes.summary: Slice 2: production schema extraction and multi-request protocol proof
nodes.detail: Carry the schema-extraction proof into production, evaluate schema metadata without facts, bind a heterogeneous root, load runtime facts and run one multi-request host program; carry unions, optionals, exact amounts and references through disk/host/guest/browser with canonical round trips, and measure whole-root costs.

realised.evidence: ADT codecs (#6), metadata (#12), structural checks (#13), query reads (#27); a live multi-request host continuation arrives only with PR #96. No browser leg exists

nodes.summary: Slice 3: reporting KB evolution loop through Web and MCP
nodes.detail: Implement evaluate/check/inspect on a synthetic reporting model with Web and MCP surfaces, human/agent review of the same differences, policy-only and schema-changing evolutions, a multi-request evolution entry with no guest Propose call, a Before-Mid-After migration, and EvolutionRejected cases for malformed observation chains.

realised.evidence: Chain rejection and candidates landed for the CLI (seq 33-36), but no reporting KB, Web or MCP surface was ever built and evolutions became pure

nodes.summary: Slice 4: acceptance, reopen and Git race/crash cases
nodes.detail: Implement acceptance and reopen with Git races, crash cases and deletion; reopen record history from archived step reports without guest execution, and verify acceptance stores the evaluated report rather than a later-edited file.

realised.evidence: PR #42 composes evolution acceptance with explicit checkout recovery; archives from #40. Per-record history reopening was not built

nodes.summary: Slice 5: vendored tap plugins, named instances, secrets, paged evidence
nodes.detail: Vendor and locally compile an independent tap plugin with two named instances of one connector type plus another plugin, prove instance selection with shared/different secrets and config isolation, acquire paged evidence and repeat curation without duplicate knowledge, and rebuild offline from vendored source.

realised.evidence: Plugin source install (#87-#90), two-instance configuration (#100/#101), curation (#111), local secrets (#122) and paged Graph calendar acquisition (#147)

nodes.summary: Slice 6: renderer-to-file-sink output path with zero browsing sink calls
nodes.detail: Prove ADR 0017's output path: a renderer composes several queries over one root into a first-party file sink's exact input, the sink is invoked explicitly and bytes verified, browsing makes no sink calls, and relative destinations resolve against the KB directory.

realised.evidence: No renderer or sink code exists in kyyn-v2

nodes.summary: First build is a CLI todo journey through the real kernel
nodes.detail: The first implementation is a CLI journey through the real kernel and MicroHs (load-compile-validate, evolution, saved-candidate checking, local acceptance/reopen) using the todo walkthrough as fixture; it explicitly does not discharge the reporting, Web/MCP, performance or distribution proofs.

realised.evidence: PR #44 exposes the first evolution journey through the CLI and closes #3

nodes.summary: Package DAG grows inside working PRs, not a scaffolding PR
nodes.detail: Establish the package DAG and signatures inside the first working CLI PR, creating only packages needed for real operations with builds/tests at each merge, never a separate scaffold or a native-Haskell stand-in for guest execution.

realised.evidence: PR #6 introduces packages alongside real MicroHs codec tests rather than an empty scaffold

nodes.summary: Composed migration test uses only Before/After endpoint contracts
nodes.detail: The slice-3 composed migration becomes a Before edit, Before-to-After migration and After edit, each with its own step report but no declared intermediate schema.

realised.evidence: PR #58 adds editBefore/evolve/editAfter and updates the Migrate journey fixture

nodes.summary: Next slice chosen from real journeys; ordering lives in issues
nodes.detail: The permanent ordered roadmap is removed: build complete paths, pick each next slice from a real user journey, and keep sequencing in issues. Coverage obligations move to an end-to-end verification checklist by area.

realised.evidence: From the CLI journey onward work was already issue-driven and ignored the reporting-first slice order

editorial.note: Also converts header to front matter and rewrites the basis line; metadata only
Desired-state reconcile: drops status/date/basis and rewords the paging caveat in Alternatives and consequences; no change in requirements

notes: This lane was mostly a roadmap: about two-thirds of the founding text was six ordered implementation slices. The real project departed from that order at seq 4 (a CLI todo journey replaced the reporting-first, Web/MCP-first slice 3), and seq 142 deleted the whole roadmap, saying ordering belongs in issues. I gave each slice a node because the section is neither Context, Consequences nor Verification, and the slices show clearly what was skipped. Slice 3 (reporting KB through Web and MCP) and slice 6 (renderer to file sink) were never built, and nothing in the new End-to-end verification list is tracked as a node, because Verification sections produce none. Slices 2, 4 and 5 were reached piecemeal and out of order (plugins and secrets well before outputs). I was unsure whether the slice nodes should count as decisions at all; if they should not, the lane comes down to 0021.01-03, 0021.10 and 0021.12.
